Present: Mr. Vipin Mahajan, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Mohit Chaudhary, Aag, Punjab.
Mr. Nitish Bhatia, Advocate for the complainant.
Sandeep Moudgil, J (Qral)

The instant petition under Section 438 Cr.P.C., has been filed for quashing of the FIR No.145, dated 10.12.2015, under Sections 420 & 120-B of the IPC, 1860,
registered at Police Station City Fazilka, District Fazilka, Punjab with all consequential proceedings qua the petitioner including the order dated 15.02.2020 (Annexure P-5) passed by Ld. CJM/Fazilka vide which the cancellation report filed by the police has been rejected as also the order dated 21.09.2022 (Anneuxre P-6).
Today during the course of hearing, a copy of the settlement/agreement dated 16.03.2023 entered into between both the parties before the Mediation and Conciliation Centre of this Court has been produced.
A perusal of the terms of agreement crystallized as under:
I.

The present CRM-M-No.2089 of 2023 (O&M) arises out of monetary dispute Mahip Trehan vs State Of Punjab And Another on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112612315/
1 between the parties.

sentences.text:
FIR No.145 dated 10.12.2015 under Sections 420-120-B of IPC,
Police 2023.03.24 09:05 | attest to the accuracy and integrity of this document Station City Fazilka, District Fazilka (Punjab) was got registered by the second party -- Jaskaran Singh (Complainant) against the first party -- Mahip Trehan.
As per the FIR, the money involved is to the tune of Rs.2,00,000/- (Two Lakh).

2. Pursuant to this FIR the parties met in the good office of SP(D) District, Fazilka, where a compromise was arrived at and sum of Rs.1,15,000/- (One Lakh fifteen thousand only) was paid to the second party.
Subsequently, the second party raised demand of Rs.85,000/- (Eighty Five Thousand) for which the matter was referred to the Mediation Centre vide order dated 09.02.2023 passed by this Hon'ble Court.

3. Detailed discussions were held with the parties and now, the parties have, with the intervention of learned advocates of both the parties voluntarily arrived at an amicable solution resolving their disputes and differences.

In addition to the already paid amount of Rs.1,15,000/- (One Lakh Fifteen Thousand) the first party undertakes to make another amount of Rs.55,000/-(Fifty Five Thousand)
as full and final payment so as to resolve the pending dispute.

This amount of Rs.55,000/- (Fifty Five Thousand) shall be paid by way of demand draft in the name of second party or in cash before this Hon'ble Court on 22.03.2023 when the present petition is fixed for hearing.
A quashing petition pertaining to this FIR is also pending before the Hon'ble Court for 22.03.2023.

On receiving the balance amount of Rs.55,000/- (fifty Five thousand) second party to undertakes to make a statement to this effect and give no objection in case of quashing of the FIR by this Hon'ble Court as his entire amount stands paid.
MEENU 4.

The parties hereto confirm and declare that they have 2023.03.24 09:05 | attest to the accuracy and integrity of this document voluntarily and of their own free will arrived at this Settlement/Agreement in the presence of the Mediator.
5. That this is the full and final settlement between the parties regarding their financial dispute.

None of the parties will claim over and above the present settled amount.
6. That the parties shall not breach the terms of settlement and if any party goes out of the terms of settlement then the other party shall have a right to take course of law.
7.

By signing this Agreement the parties hereto state that they have no further claims or demands against each other and all the disputes and differences in this regard have been amicably settled by the parties hereto through the process of Conciliation/Mediation and the parties shall not institute any other case against each other will respect to the present claim.
Both the parties also undertakes not to initiate any further litigation on the same subject matter in future.

MEENU Full Bench of this Court in Kulwinder Singh and others vs. State 2023.03.24 09:05 | attest to the accuracy and integrity of this document of Punjab, 2007 (3) RCR (Criminal) 1052, has held:-
"The only inevitable conclusion from the above discussion is that there is no statutory bar under the Cr.P.C. which can affect the inherent power of this Court under Section 482.

sentences.text: Further, the same cannot be limited to matrimonial cases alone and the Court has the wide power to quash the proceedings even in noncompoundable offences notwithstanding the bar under Section 320 of the CrPC., in order to prevent the abuse of law and to secure the ends of justice.
The power under Section 482 of the CrP.C. is to be exercised Ex-Debitia Justitia to prevent an abuse of process of Court.
There can neither be an exhaustive list nor the defined para-meters to enable a High Court to invoke or exercise its inherent powers.
It will always depend upon the facts and circumstances of each case.
The power under Section 482 of the CrP.C. has no limits.
However, the High Court will exercise it sparingly and with utmost care and caution.
The exercise of power has to be with circumspection and restraint.
The Court is a vital and an extra-ordinary effective instrument to maintain and control social order.
The Courts play role of paramount importance in achieving peace, harmony and ever- lasting congeniality in society.

Resolution of a dispute by way of a compromise between two warring groups,
therefore, should attract the immediate and prompt attention of a Court which should endeavour to give full effect to the same unless such compromise is abhorrent to lawful composition of the society or would promote savagery."

The legal principles as laid down for quashing of the judgment were also approved by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of 'Gian Singh Versus State of Punjab and another,(2012) 10 SCC 303'.
Furthermore, MEENU 2023.03.24 09:05 | attest to the accuracy and integrity of this document the broad principles for exercising the powers under Section 482 were summarized by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of ''Parbatbhai Aahir @ Parbatbhai_ Bhimsinhbhai_ Karmur and others versus State of Gujarat and another" (2017) 9 SCC 641'.

The furtherance of the proceedings is likely to be a waste of judicial time and there appears to be no chances of conviction.
Keeping in view the case law discussed hereinabove and the settlement arrived at between the parties in the agreement dated 16.03.2023, the present petition is allowed.
In view of above, FIR (Annexure P-1), with all the consequential proceedings arising therefrom, is quashed qua the petitioner.
